title: Three-term iterated Hom differential on one tensor summand
statement: Let C be a site, R a sheaf of commutative rings, and K,L,M cochain complexes of R-modules. Use the chosen Hom complex and projections [def-pur-hom-complex] and degreewise currying a_n [lem-sc-hom-tensor-degreewise]. Put T=Tot(K tensor L) [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For integers n,t,p,q with p+q=t, let ι:K^p tensor L^q→T^t be the summand inclusion, and let d1,d2:K^p tensor L^q→T^(t+1) be the first and signed second summand differentials. After restriction by internalHom(ι,id), d_iterated a_(n+1) π_(n+1,t) equals a_n π_(n,t) internalHom(ι,d_M) minus (-1)^n a_n π_(n,t+1) internalHom(d1,id) minus (-1)^n a_n π_(n,t+1) internalHom(d2,id). Here d1 sends x tensor y to d_K x tensor y, while d2 sends it to (-1)^p x tensor d_L y. This statement concerns one summand only, with separate differential contributions.

source.place: Lemma sites-cohomology-lemma-compose (Tag 0A90), referring to More on Algebra Tag 0A5Y

proof.text: Use the defining currying equation [lem-sc-hom-tensor-degreewise] at n+1, then the outer Hom differential projection identity [def-pur-hom-complex]. Evaluate on localized sections x of K^p and y of L^q: the postcomposition term applies the inner differential to f(x); the precomposition term is minus (-1)^n f(d_K x)(y). Apply the inner Hom projection identity to the first term, giving d_M(f(x)(y)) minus (-1)^(p+n) f(x)(d_L y).

The tensor summand maps d1 and d2 have the values stated above [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Identify the degree-n evaluations using the currying equation [lem-sc-hom-tensor-degreewise]. The integer sign identity (-1)^(p+n)=(-1)^n*(-1)^p makes the localized calculation exactly the three-term formula, with d2 already carrying the sign (-1)^p. This identity also holds for negative n,p.

Bilinearity extends the calculation on pure tensors to the presheaf tensor. The sheafification adjunction and tensor-Hom adjunction [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] extend equality to the sheaf tensor on each localized site, hence to the internal Hom factor of this summand. No coproduct assembly or combination of d1 and d2 is claimed here. If K,L,M or their differentials vanish the same computation gives zero terms.

theorem homTensorDegreewiseMap_iteratedDifferential_summand
    (K L M : CochainComplex Mod ℤ) (n t p q : ℤ) (h : p + q = t) :
    letI := SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory R
    let T := CochainComplex.mapBifunctor K L (curriedTensor Mod)
    let ι := CochainComplex.ιMapBifunctor K L (curriedTensor Mod) p q t h
    (homComplex (R := R) K (homComplex (R := R) L M)).d n (n + 1) ≫
        homTensorDegreewiseMap R K L M (n + 1) ≫
          homTensorProjection R T M (n + 1) t (t + (n + 1)) rfl ≫
            SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := R) ι (𝟙 (M.X (t + (n + 1)))) =
      (homTensorDegreewiseMap R K L M n ≫
        homTensorProjection R T M n t (t + n) rfl ≫
          SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := R) ι (M.d (t + n) (t + (n + 1)))) -
      n.negOnePow • (homTensorDegreewiseMap R K L M n ≫
        homTensorProjection R T M n (t + 1) (t + (n + 1)) (by omega) ≫
          SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := R)
            (HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor.d₁ K L (curriedTensor Mod)
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ) p q (t + 1)) (𝟙 (M.X (t + (n + 1))))) -
      n.negOnePow • (homTensorDegreewiseMap R K L M n ≫
        homTensorProjection R T M n (t + 1) (t + (n + 1)) (by omega) ≫
          SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := R)
            (HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor.d₂ K L (curriedTensor Mod)
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ) p q (t + 1)) (𝟙 (M.X (t + (n + 1)))))
